transcript:
Header
Date: 2026-07-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 min
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Alvarez (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Verdant Head of ML), Tom Reeves (Verdant Platform Eng), Priya Patel (Verdant Finance)

Summary: Quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Customer wants to understand per-route unit economics, SLOs, and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for a 500k tokens/day pilot.
Topics: console demo, per-route dashboards, cost allocation, rollouts and canaries, Private deployment requirements, compliance docs, next steps and pricing

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, this should be about 45 minutes, we'll do a short demo of the console and then q a and next steps
[00:08] Maya (Verdant): great thanks Sofia, we really wanted to see route-level cost and how you break down embeddings vs generative token costs, and also how to map that back to our business metrics
[00:15] Ethan (Redwood SE): cool, i'll share my screen, bear with me while i pull up the Verdant demo tenant, ok slides link in chat as well: https://redwood.ai/demo/verdant-console
[00:28] Tom (Verdant): small noise, can you also show alerting on latency and cost spikes? that's a must for ops
[00:35] Ethan: yep we'll get there, first page is the usage overview, you can see token consumption trend, cost by model family, and high level per-route traffic
[01:02] Ethan: so you can filter by route, e g product-recs, customer-support, and batch-embedding jobs, and the console will show token counts, avg latency, and cost per 1k tokens
[01:30] Priya (Finance): how accurate are those cost numbers, are you using list price or our committed discount?
[01:36] Sofia: good q, in the hosted plan we show both raw unit price and effective price after any discount or reserved capacity. For Dedicated we show amortized infra cost plus model compute cost, so it is more reflective of your actual spend
[02:05] Maya: ok and what about route-level SLOs, can we set different latency targets for product-recs vs checkout flows?
[02:12] Ethan: yes, per-route SLOs are first-class, you can set p95 targets and a cost budget. The console will show days-to-burn at current rate and alert if you exceed a threshold
[02:45] Maya: nice, and if we need strict isolation we were looking at Private, what does that change from the console side?
[02:51] Sofia: Private gives you a control plane in your VPC and you manage networking. The console still surfaces the same dashboards via the private control plane. For security we integrate with your KMS and SSO, and we ship audit logs back to your S3 or syslog
[03:20] Tom: about KMS, do you support customer-managed keys in HSM? we need that for PCI-ish flows
[03:26] Ethan: yes, we support cloud KMS providers and HSM integrations for Private deployments. We'll share the network guide and KMS matrix after this call
[03:55] Priya: on costs, show us an example of per-route cost allocation to product teams, we want to chargeback product lines
[04:02] Ethan: switching to per-route dashboard, here you can tag routes with team, business unit, and the cost table will break down compute, storage (cache hits), and embedding costs per tag
[04:30] Ethan: note we also show cache hit rate and KV cache savings, so if your prefix caching is doing well you can see the token savings and dollar savings next to the route
[05:00] Maya: does Redwood recommend specific quantization/batching settings per route? we have some low-latency checkout paths and some heavy embeddings workloads
[05:08] Sofia: yes, that's part of Redwood Optimize. For low-latency routes we recommend lighter quantization and aggressive per-request batching disabled, for high-throughput embeddings we recommend int8 quantization and larger batch profiles. We'll attach a sample Optimize config in the follow up
[05:40] Tom: what's the typical latency for a small chat request on Dedicated versus Hosted? ballpark numbers are fine
[05:46] Ethan: on Dedicated with pinned GPU pools we routinely hit 30-60ms for a 128-token generation p95 depending on model and kernel, hosted can be similar but depends on multi-tenant burst capacity, and you can also choose region and lower latency by reserving closer capacity
[06:18] Maya: you said 30-60 ms p95, that seems optimistic, any caveats?
[06:22] Ethan: yeah fair, those numbers are for optimized models on A100 / H100 class hardware and with KV cache warming; for cold starts or larger sequence lengths expect higher 100s of ms or seconds for large context loads
[06:50] Priya: can we get a breakdown in the console of cost per 1k tokens by model variant? e g base model vs quantized 4-bit variant
[06:58] Ethan: yes the model cost view shows list price and effective cost by variant, and you can run cost-simulations to see impact of switching variants for a route over a historical period
[07:25] Maya: are there built-in rollouts? we need canary and automatic fallback to cheaper models if latency spikes
[07:30] Sofia: yep rollouts are supported, you can do canary percentages and automatic fallback policies based on latency or error rates; the console shows the rollout and recent metrics inline
[07:55] Tom: one of our big concerns is observability. do the dashboards link back to traces for a single request?
[08:00] Ethan: every token request has a trace id, you can click from a failed request to the trace and see the route, model, kernel selection, and timing breakdown per stage
[08:18] Maya: ok nice, that helps debug KV cache misses and batching inefficiencies
[08:30] Ethan: also, we surface token-level cost and latency attribution so you can see which part of the request consumed the tokens and which were cached
[09:00] Sofia: quick demo of cost explorer, i'm going to filter to last 30 days and show cost by route, and then drill into product-recs route
[09:20] Sofia: you can see a spike on July 15th, click the spike and it shows which client keys and routes contributed, and the console can auto-suggest throttle rules or batching changes
[09:48] Priya: can the console export cost-allocation csvs for finance?
[09:52] Ethan: yes csv and we also push to your billing S3. You can schedule monthly exports and integrate with your internal chargeback system
[10:10] Maya: do you have built-in alerts for anomalies in cost like sudden token inflation due to prompt changes?
[10:16] Ethan: yes anomaly detection is part of usage analytics, you can tune sensitivity and get slack/email alerts, it also surfaces sample requests that triggered the anomaly for quick triage
[10:40] Tom: our infra folks worry about networking for Private, specifically VPC peering and egress costs, can you summarize what we need
[10:47] Sofia: we'll send the network architecture guide, but short answer: Private uses customer VPC with a control plane that can be in your account or a Redwood-managed control plane in a partner region, egress patterns depend on if you use on-prem model serving or cloud GPUs; we'll include cost examples in the follow up
[11:20] Maya: timeline-wise, we want to land a pilot in Q3, measure latency and cost over 30 days, and then decide on Dedicated or Private by Q4
[11:30] Sofia: that's doable. Pilot usually is 2-4 weeks to get traffic shaping and caching tuned, then a 30 day measurement period is ideal
[11:40] Priya: ok show us a sample pilot pricing scenario quickly
[11:43] Sofia: sure, for 500k tokens/day with a mixed workload we have two options: hosted with committed discount or Dedicated with 3 month commit. Hosted is faster to start, Dedicated gives better unit economics at scale. I'll send a numbers table after the call
[12:05] Ethan: back to console features, the per-route dashboard also supports custom metrics import so you can correlate revenue events with model cost
[12:30] Maya: do you support tagging requests with user ids so we can link to customer lifetime value?
[12:35] Ethan: yes, request metadata allows custom tags and the analytics engine will roll up by tag and include e g user cohort metrics
[12:55] Tom: any red flags for compliance? we need SOC 2 and ISO proof before procurement signs off
[12:59] Sofia: we are SOC 2 Type II and have ISO documentation, for Private deployments we can provide architecture reviews and audit logs. We'll attach certs and a security checklist in the follow up
[13:20] Maya: also legal wants to know about data residency for EU customers
[13:25] Ethan: we have region controls and can pin serving to EU regions and support customer-managed logs in-region, we'll include the data residency section in the security pack
[13:50] Priya: ok what about disaster recovery and failover between regions?
[13:55] Sofia: we support multi-region routing and automated fallback to a secondary region. For critical paths we recommend Dedicated with cross-region replication for the KV cache
[14:20] Maya: can you demonstrate the per-route drilldown showing a specific failed request and the stack trace?
[14:24] Ethan: yep clicking into a sample failed request now, here's the request header, the model variant selected, and the kernel timings, you can see an elevated tokenization cost due to a long input string
[14:50] Maya: ah we have a lot of long customer support threads, can prefix caching help reduce that?
[14:56] Ethan: absolutely, prefix/KV cache is designed for repeated contexts, you'll see savings in both latency and cost for repeated customer threads
[15:15] Tom: any integration work for our observability stack, we run Datadog and Splunk
[15:20] Sofia: we have direct exporters and you can also forward audit logs to your splunk ingest; we'll add an integration checklist to the follow up
[15:55] Priya: about the cost simulation, can we run a what-if for converting 25% of requests to a smaller quantized model and see the savings?
[16:00] Ethan: yes the cost simulator lets you set a percent traffic shift and a time window, and then calculates projected savings and impacts to latency and error rates
[16:30] Maya: do you keep a history of model regressions tied to prompts and evals? we need to make sure quality doesn't drop if we switch variants
[16:36] Sofia: Redwood Optimize ties quality monitoring to prompt sets, you can set regression alerts and tie them to rollbacks if quality drops beyond a threshold
[16:55] Tom: for the pilot we want a small set of eval prompts and a regression threshold; can Redwood run continuous evals on our traffic?
[17:00] Ethan: yes we can run continuous evals against your prompt set in the console and surface quality trends alongside cost metrics
[17:25] Maya: one practical ask: show me how to set a budget alert for product-recs route that pings Slack when daily spend exceeds 5% of monthly budget
[17:30] Ethan: demoing budgets now, create budget, tie to route tag product-recs, set threshold 5 percent, choose slack channel and alert cadence, done
[17:55] Priya: procurement will ask about discounts for committed volume, how reasonable are those?
[18:00] Sofia: typical discounts increase with commit length and capacity size. For 500k tokens/day on a 12 month commit we can move the per-token price materially, i'll include a couple pricing scenarios in the follow up
[18:30] Maya: are there any hidden costs like egress or storage?
[18:35] Ethan: egress depends on your cloud and whether you use Private with data egress in your account; storage for KV cache is small but we show it in the cost table so there are no surprises
[19:00] Tom: ok let's talk pilot scope, we want to include product-recs and customer-support routes, run for 30 days, and measure cost, latency, and quality
[19:10] Sofia: noted. pilot scope: product-recs + support, 30 day measure, dedicated benchmark and optimize tuning. we'll prepare the SOW and pricing options
[19:30] Maya: timeline again, can we get the SOW and pricing by next week?
[19:35] Sofia: yes we'll aim to have pricing and SOW by 2026-08-02
[19:50] Priya: finance would like a CSV with route-level cost and tags for month to send to accounting
[19:55] Ethan: will include a sample csv export and the automated export setup in the doc set
[20:10] Sofia: quick run through of security docs link in chat, and i'll mark the action items now
[20:20] Sofia: p.s. there was a question about competitor comparisons earlier, we typically see customers evaluate OpenAI for simplicity, Anthropic for safety features, and in-house for cost control, but end up choosing a mix depending on latency and compliance needs
[20:45] Maya: any rough numbers on ROI for caching and quantization changes?
[20:50] Ethan: we have case studies showing 30-60 percent cost reduction for heavy caching workloads and 20-40 percent savings from quantization in embedding-heavy workloads; exact numbers depend on your traffic profile
[21:15] Priya: ok that's helpful, thanks
[21:20] Sofia: any other questions?
[21:25] Maya: not right now, we'll follow up after we review the docs
[21:30] Sofia: great, recap next steps: pricing and SOW, security pack, benchmark plan, schedule pilot onboarding. thanks everyone

End of transcript
